arm_id.description: CT.gov results group id (OG000), disambiguated when CT.gov reuses it for a genuinely different arm in another outcome measure: '{raw_id}#{analysis_population}', or '{raw_id}#2', '{raw_id}#3', ... when the reused id's OMs share the same analysis_population too. Unique within this trial; an id with no collision is left exactly as CT.gov wrote it -- see atlas.results.build_arm_id_map

role.description: curated; CT.gov armGroups[].type is unreliable -- a trial can label its own placebo arm EXPERIMENTAL

analysis_population.description: the outcome measure this arm entry was first seen in; the disambiguator baked into arm_id when it collided

arms.description: per-trial arm registry from CT.gov results groups, role-classified

verbatim_sha1.description: sha1 hex digest of the referenced endpoint's verbatim; guards the join against a silent position shift

endpoint.description: Reference to endpoints.<rank>_endpoints[position-1]; never re-describes the endpoint

denominator.description: participants analyzed in this arm for this measure

reported_unit.description: CT.gov unitOfMeasure verbatim (4 casings exist in the corpus -- do not parse it, use value_type to disambiguate count vs. rate)

responders.description: count; null when the source posted only a rate, never back-computed

response_rate_pct.description: 0-100; null unless the measure is a responder rate

rate_is_derived.description: true when response_rate_pct was computed as responders/denominator rather than posted directly

ctgov_class_title.description: the classes[].title the timepoint was parsed from, e.g. 'Week 16' -- provenance for the timepoint binding

items.description: One row per endpoint x timepoint x arm (a CT.gov results measurement)

arm_results.description: one row per endpoint x timepoint x arm (CT.gov results)

effect_type.description: null when the raw label maps to none of the 8 canonical types

verbatim.description: CT.gov pValue string exactly as posted, e.g. '< 0.0001'

p_value.description: P-value as bound + value; reuses the ScoreCriterion comparator idiom
